In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the students in the high completion departments were more likely to be socialized into the discipline and into the institution than students in low completion departments.

the socialization experiences of doctoral students in low completion departments are more likely to include: (a) more negative and stressful experiences, (b) less positive and supportive experiences, (c) less frequent and less positive experiences with faculty, (d) less frequent and more negative experiences with peers, (e) less frequent and negative experiences with administrators, and (f) less frequent and positive experiences with students.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students in low completion departments experience a lack of socialization and a sense of isolation that is not present among students in high completion departments.

students in high completion departments were more likely to experience a more positive, supportive socialization experience, which was more likely to occur in the later developmental phases of the students' experience.

the socialization process in high-completion departments is more likely to include the development of a community of scholars, a sense of belonging, and a shared sense of responsibility for the students' success.
The main takeaway from our work is that
doctoral socialization is a dynamic, complex process that is influenced by the departmental context and the individual student's experiences within that context.
doctoral students in high-completing departments have a better chance of completing their degrees in 5-6 years than their counterparts in low-completing departments.
the socialization process is not uniform, but rather, varies based on the departmental context in which it is embedded.
